admission.justification: Avoids dismissing a gate or choosing the row when the user intended only to dismiss its overdue inbox entry.

applicability: An overdue handover inbox dismissal inside an Operations row.
conditions: Pointer-down and click isolation prevent the ListBox from selecting the row.
The inbox control remains reachable and explicitly names chat when a gate owns the word.
exclusions: Sending gate dismissal from the inbox control.

evidence: dashboard/src/panels/lifecycle-list/signals.test.tsx: "offers the dismissal of an overdue hand-over beside the word, and it does not choose the row" and "keeps the dismissal of an overdue hand-over reachable while an open gate is the row's word"; dashboard/src/panels/lifecycle-list/rowState.test.ts: "says the most pressing fact as the one word"; fault runs gate-keeps-dismissal, dismissal-named and pickup-press-reaches-row (notes/reports/worker/8c3d5f2a-6e74-4b90-c2f1-144000000a01/role-launch/evidence-L144-A2/103-fault-runs-final.log); sandbox tries pressOnDismiss and gateAndOverdueHandOver in notes/run3/operations-sidebar-proposal/comparison/probe.json; comparison page, section "An open gate and an overdue hand-over on the same task" (state stood in) and its difference "An overdue hand-over on a task that also has an open gate". Repair of the Reviewer's finding L144-R1-03.

origin.handoffEntry: MIK-R144@v1 rule 5 / a control inside a row

statement: A control inside a row keeps its press from the list, because the list chooses a row when a press starts and not at the click; the dismissal of an overdue hand-over therefore dismisses and does not choose the row. It is offered whenever the hand-over is overdue: as "×" beside "check chat" while the hand-over is the row's word, and as "chat ×" beside the gate's word while an open gate is the row's word, named so that it cannot be read as a dismissal of the gate; it sends the dismissal of the hand-over's inbox entry and nothing for the gate.
